title: I Used the Call-Center After-Call Work Timer on the Team Lead

parts.text: I wrapped a call at 3:41 p.m. and used the two minutes of after-call work the handbook allowed. Team Lead Chris pulled me back to ready at 3:42 because the queue was red. I was twenty-four, year two, notes half-typed. Chris's own dashboard, visible on the shared wall, showed he sat in ACW for eleven minutes after a call with his mother, which the system labeled inbound. I screenshotted the wall, the handbook two-minute line, and my truncated notes. Then I stayed in ACW until 3:43. At 3:44 Chris posted that some people game timers.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He posted about gaming timers with eleven minutes of inbound-mom still on the wall.

social.video_title: He yanked my two minutes with eleven of his on the wall — Part 1/2
social.description: Queue red, notes half-typed, inbound mom. The wall does not blink. Would you have gone ready?

parts.text: QA asked for both screenshots. My notes finished. Chris's inbound got a coaching. The wall still shows numbers. Two minutes returned to being two. I take them. Mothers can call cell phones. Queues being red is not a handbook amendment. I clock the timer like it is mine, because the PDF says it is. Headset stays on. Gaming is a word leads use for arithmetic.

social.video_title: QA can do arithmetic too — Part 2/2
social.description: Notes finished, coaching issued, two minutes restored. Was mom a queue?
